evaluation.limitation: One selected historical external UART defect, not a held-out benchmark or new discovery. Twelve finite serial/flow checks plus two bounded CTS properties. Small-divisor and computed-parity modes excluded after pre-inference maintainer-control qualification. No fixed RTL used for scoring.

proposal.explanation: The RTL meets the CTS-specific behavioral contract. The CTS synchronizer (two flip-flops) provides the required latency; after a receiver blocks for eight clocks, the transmitter's busy remains high and no new byte is accepted. Reset and BREAK enforce a 16-baud recovery period. Byte acceptance occurs on i_wr && !o_busy outside reset/BREAK. Configuration is held constant between bytes. The excluded issues (divisor-two forward-progress and computed-parity disagreement) are not part of this CTS contract. No changes are required.

proposal.explanation: The violation occurred because after BREAK recovery the transmitter momentarily cleared busy (r_busy=0) regardless of CTS status, creating a one-cycle window where a byte could be accepted while the receiver continuously blocked. The fix changes the TXU_BREAK block to set r_busy based on the synchronized CTS (ck_cts) so that when hardware flow control is enabled and the receiver is blocked (ck_cts=0), busy remains high after the 16-baud recovery interval.
